keyFindings.description: The pull request conflicts with its base. gh pr view reports mergeable CONFLICTING and mergeStateStatus DIRTY; main is 5 commits ahead of this head, the newest being 'chore: release pi-legion v10.16.0 [skip ci]', and nine files are touched by both sides since the merge base 2127101bddff: packages/pi-legion/package.json, packages/pi-legion/AGENTS.md, packages/claude-envoy/{package.json,CHANGELOG.md,dist/envoy-channel.js}, packages/contracts/fixtures/daemon-api/version.json, packages/daemon/internal/api/version.go, docs/site/src/content/docs/legion/running-legion.md and scripts/e2e/README.md. Nothing in the change is wrong; this is the forge state, and it is the whole of this round's verdict. An approval now would be worth nothing twice over: GitHub computes no merge ref for a conflicting head and runs no on: pull_request workflow for any of its activity, so no later head of this branch gets checks until the conflict is cured, and the forward merge that cures it lands above the approved commit, which READY then refuses as READY_UNREVIEWED_CHANGE. The remedy is the forward merge, not a rebase: merge main into the issue branch, resolve each of the nine by hand, push, and the round after reviews the merge itself.
keyFindings.nextRound: This verdict is a request for changes, so the round after it continues against the new head rather than being a fingerprint confirmation. If the forward merge is a pure union and the unchanged-diff fingerprint is unchanged, that round is the approval and needs no second full audit: everything below is already cleared at this head and only the merge itself has to be read.

clearedAtThisHead.finding1TheGuardIsNowPinned: Verified by my own mutation, and I confirmed the mutation was applied before reading its result — the lesson your tester volunteered, which I had the chance to learn the same way ten minutes later. I reverted plugins.go to the pre-guard shape, printed the rendered block to see the old shape in place, then ran the new test: exactly one subtest fails, 'a regular file an interrupted flock left behind', with the message naming the consequence; 'a cache already filled', 'a symlink to a filled cache' and 'no cache at all' all stay green. That is the narrow failure I asked for — a test that went red everywhere would pin the wrapper rather than the guard. plugins.go restored, working copy clean.
clearedAtThisHead.theDocumentationFence: Verified the same way, and my first attempt at it failed exactly as the implementer's first version of the fence did: my mutation did not apply (the path I struck was not in the region I searched), the tests passed, and the pass was mine rather than the fence's. I read the lists, struck the '- `/legion/uv/cache`' item from the delete list for real, confirmed the list no longer carries it, and reran: TestTheReclaimParagraphNamesEveryDirectoryTheRendererPutsOnTheIssueVolume fails with 'accounts for /legion/uv/cache in neither list, though the renderer puts it on the issue's volume: it belongs on the delete list or in an exemption, and a mention inside an exemption's reason is neither' — the message names the exact false-pass hole the first version had. The companion test stays green, which is right: striking a path is not a collision.
clearedAtThisHead.finding2TheTmpWindow: Answered and correctly scoped: the paragraph now says tmp's only creator is a role's next shim start through podsafety.EnsureScratch, that a shim lives across turns so a tmp deleted under a live role stays gone until relaunch, that mktemp -d fails with exit 1 where Python's tempfile silently falls back to /tmp — the container filesystem charged to the limit this layout exists to escape — and that tmp is therefore deleted with the role stopped, not merely between turns. Both halves of what I ran are in the document, including the quiet one.
clearedAtThisHead.finding3TheUvSplit: Answered: /legion/uv/cache is on the delete list and /legion/uv/python/<issue> is exempt, with the dependency named — the interpreters uv installed, and a .venv in the issue's workspace that this remedy does not delete pointing at one of them.
clearedAtThisHead.theStructure: The paragraph is now two explicit lists rather than a prose sentence, which is the structural change that makes the fence possible at all. This is the seventh version of it and the first whose correctness does not depend on a human noticing.
